transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-08
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Priya Desai, Marco Alvarez (Redwood); Sophie Tan, Ethan Cole, Marta Ruiz, Ben Howard (WillowBank)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand WillowBank's cost sensitivity, hosting constraints (VPC/on-prem), and decision criteria for hosted vs dedicated vs private. Focus on per-token economics, batching/caching levers, and a proposed pilot for cost validation.

Topics covered:
- Current usage and expected throughput
- Latency targets vs budget tradeoffs
- Data residency / PII retention and KMS needs
- Benchmarks and pilot scope
- Next steps and pricing materials

Transcript:
[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for jumping on, i'm priya from Redwood, um, i'll hand off to marco for a quick intro on the cost models after a quick status from you folks.
[00:20] Sophie: thanks priya, quick context — we've got about 12M monthly requests across our chat+nlp pipelines, average prompt 350 tokens, responses around 120 tokens. Patty, sorry Ben will own product detail, but high level that's the ballpark.
[00:34] Ben: yes that's right, and we're forecasting growth, maybe 2x in six months depending on adoption. Budget wise, we have... rough budget cap of $90k/mo for inference initially.
[00:48] Marco: got it. so first, small note on terminology — when we say per-token it's really invoiced per-1k tokens in Redwood hosted; dedicated pricing is usually a combination of reserved node cost + a lower per-token unit. that is, you trade fixed vs variable.
[01:05] Ethan: quick question — what's the typical delta between hosted per-token and dedicated unit cost? ballpark.
[01:12] Marco: ballpark depends a lot on batchability and model size. For a high-batch workload that uses prefix caching, we've seen effective unit cost drop 30-60% on dedicated vs single-tenant hosted, but that assumes you can fill the GPU and use continuous batching. if you have low qps or lots of short-lived sessions it's more modest.
[01:35] Marta: and security — we are regulated, SOC two plus an internal audit. we need KMS integration, SSO (we use SAML2), audit logs, and ability to limit data residency. would hosted cover that?
[01:49] Priya: hosted can offer SOC 2, KMS integration via customer-managed keys, and audit logs; for strict residency or air-gapped needs we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated inside a VPC. note: sometimes our auto redact/purge delays are misunderstood — if you need no retention at all we can configure policies but private gives most control.
[02:12] Sophie: what about KV cash — sorry cache — the prefix cache, how big an impact does that have?
[02:19] Marco: KV cache is huge for chat-style workloads. with good session affinity and prefix caching you avoid recomputing large parts of the context which reduces token generation and latency. In cost terms, cache + batching can cut per-session token consumption by 20-40% in practice, depends on repetitiveness.
[02:36] Sophie: if we go hosted, do we still get batching benefits?
[02:40] Marco: yes — Redwood hosted supports continuous batching and prefix caching. The difference is you share pools with other tenants so your ability to sustain very high optimized batching depends on traffic patterns; that's where dedicated pools help — consistent throughput and reserved capacity.
[02:55] Ethan: around pricing mechanics — do you bill for input+output? or only output?
[02:59] Priya: both input and output tokens — that's standard. We show both in dashboards so you can see where tokens are spent.
[03:05] Ben: do you support quantization or smaller model variants for cost saving?
[03:10] Marco: yes, we support quantized model variants and smaller family models. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization levels and batching configs per workload. careful: quantization can affect quality so we tie it to evals and regression alerts.
[03:26] Sophie: timeline — we have a board decision end of feb, and procurement needs vendor security pack by mid-jan. we'd like a quick pilot so we can bring numbers to the board.
[03:38] Priya: good, that's realistic. proposed pilot: 2-week hosted pilot using a representative prompt set to collect token counts & latency. Alternately, a short dedicated pilot (reserved slice for 48h) to show best-case unit economics. which would you prefer?
[03:56] Sophie: product prefers hosted pilot to move faster, security would prefer dedicated/VPC for auditability. we may need both — start hosted to gather usage then run a 48h dedicated benchmark.
[04:12] Marta: also need assurance around logs — does hosted redact PII automatically? we have credit card numbers and some ssn fragments in debug traces occasionally.
[04:22] Marco: hosted has configurable redaction and we can apply pre-send sanitizers in the SDK; for absolute control private/dedicated inside your VPC is recommended. we'll include the exact controls in the security pack.
[04:34] Ethan: on math — can you show a worked example? 12M requests, average 470 tokens total (in+out) what's a rough monthly spend hosted vs dedicated?
[04:46] Marco: quick rough math — assume hosted $0.0009 per token (example), that's ~ $4k per M tokens so 12M * 470 tokens => 5.64B tokens. at $0.0009 that's $5,076 — wait that's off, sorry let me re-calc. (laughter) okay, clearer: pricing usually per 1k tokens, so at $0.9 per 1k tokens is a different scale. we'll send a worked spreadsheet. the main point: you need to convert tokens to 1k units and account for batch/caching which can reduce the effective tokens.
[05:25] Ben: ha, math aside, main ask is: can you show delta if we do prefix cache + 2 configs: optimistic (40% reduction) and conservative (15% reduction)?
[05:37] Marco: yes we'll modeling both. We'll run a small simulation with your sample prompts to estimate pre- and post-cache token counts.
[05:44] Sophie: procurement — do you have standard MSSA? we need liability clauses and data processing addendum.
[05:50] Priya: yes MSSA + DPA available. we'll attach the standard docs; for enterprise deals we can negotiate specific residency language.
[06:00] Marta: also, monitoring — can we see token-level traces per route? need to attribute spend to features.
[06:06] Marco: Redwood Console provides per-route and token-level breakdowns, you can drill to user-level with proper instrumentation. We'll show screenshots in the follow-up pack.
[06:18] Ben: question about burst capacity — if traffic spikes (black friday type) do you have automatic burst options?
[06:25] Priya: yes hosted has burst buffers; dedicated can be configured with burst capacity or autoscaling policies. there's cost to burst but it's explicit — we can show typical numbers.
[06:34] Sophie: any gotchas on model switching during a rollout? we want A/B between a smaller quantized model and a larger model with fallbacks.
[06:44] Marco: Redwood supports canary rollouts, automatic fallback policies, and traffic split. We also support structured response validation to avoid obvious regressions.
[06:52] Sophie: great. last item from my side — residency question: some EU customers require data not leave EU. Can hosted handle region pinning?
[06:59] Priya: yes region pinning is possible and for stricter needs Private deployment in your VPC + KMS is the pattern.
[07:07] Ethan: can you give a sense of SLA on latency for dedicated pools?
[07:11] Marco: typical P95 latency for standard seq lengths on dedicated is 50-120ms depending on model size; we publish profiles per model. For hard real-time needs we tune serving kernels and batch windows.
[07:24] Marta: security follow-ups — we'll send the SOC 2 controls mapping we'd like you to review.
[07:31] Priya: perfect. we'll include a controls matrix in the pack.
[07:36] (short pause)
[07:40] Priya: ok to recap next steps — we will: 1) send hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet and pilot options, 2) Marco will propose a benchmark plan and run simulations using your sample prompts, 3) you'll share security checklist and confirm retention / PII constraints.
[07:58] Sophie: yes that sounds right. 1 more: can Marco include expected cost per active user, not just per-token? that's how the board wants to see it.
[08:08] Marco: yep we'll map tokens->cost->active user using your MAU numbers.
[08:13] Ben: thanks all, this was helpful. we'll regroup after the deck.
[08:18] Priya: thanks everyone, i'll follow up with the pack and calendar invite for the dedicated pricing review.

End of transcript.

Recorded notes: some transcription errors present (SAML2 transcribed as S a m l two etc), speaker labels may shift in places. Links to attachments to follow in follow up email: hosted_vs_dedicated_pricing.xlsx; security_controls_matrix.pdf; benchmark_prompt_sample.json
